cf.title: Uncancellable infinite loop in xpath() with entity references

input.subject: Uncancellable infinite loop in xpath() with entity references

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the choice of XML_PARSE_NOENT, which xml_parse() and contrib/xml2 already use. Three fixable level 2 points remain: the branch plan for a result-changing bugfix (standards-compat-2), stale expression indexes and stored values after upgrade (standards-compat-1), and whether entity reference nodes can still reach XPath (maintenance-fit-1). Only message #1 is visible, so confidence is low.

brief.title: Expand entity references in xpath(), xmlexists() and XMLTABLE
brief.problem: A query such as xpath('/r/text()/following::comment()', ...) on a document with an entity reference loops forever inside libxml2. The backend ignores cancel, statement_timeout and pg_terminate_backend(), so only kill -9 and a restart stop it. Separately, xpath() sees a different tree than the rest of the xml code, so count(//b) returns 0 where the expanded document has 2.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds XML_PARSE_NOENT to the parse calls in xpath_internal() and XmlTableSetDocument(). xml_parse() and contrib/xml2 already use this flag. Internal entities are then expanded before XPath evaluation, so no entity reference nodes stay in the tree.
user_visible_surface: xpath() returns different results for documents with entity references, e.g. /r/text() on <r>u&e;</r> gives {uy} instead of {u}.
xmlexists() evaluates against the entity-expanded document.
XMLTABLE evaluates against the entity-expanded document.
author_claims: The change fixes the uncancellable infinite loop.
xpath(), xmlexists() and XMLTABLE become consistent with xml_parse() and contrib/xml2.
The changed results are arguably an improvement.
Documents without entity references are not affected.
The root cause is most likely a libxml2 bug in xmlXPathNextFollowing, which the author plans to report.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. The entry is tagged as a bugfix, targets version 19, and needs review.
unclear: The patch does not say whether the fix is meant for back branches, given that it changes query results.
The material does not say whether XML_PARSE_NOENT adds any risk from external entities or entity expansion size in these code paths.
The material does not say which libxml2 versions show the loop.
The author does not say whether other XPath forms can still loop on documents parsed elsewhere, or whether interrupt handling inside libxml2 is addressed.
The patch has no documentation change describing the changed behaviour.

prior_attempts.title: Added support of XML_PARSE_HUGE flag for XML documents
prior_attempts.quote: The security team has discussed 2197d06224a1 after a report from coverity regarding the effects that issues like [1] would create in the backend, and concluded that this patch should be reverted because this could cause the backend to waste plently of CPU and/or memory even if the application applied checks on the size of the data given in input, and libxml2 does not offer guarantees that input limits are respected under XML_PARSE_HUGE.
prior_attempts.reason: The XML_PARSE_HUGE change was committed to HEAD as 2197d06224a1 and then reverted in f2743a7d70e7. The security team found that it lets the backend use large amounts of CPU and memory in cases like the billion laughs attack, even when the application checks input size, because libxml2 does not guarantee input limits under XML_PARSE_HUGE. The author agreed with the revert. The separate replacement of xmlSubstituteEntitiesDefault() with XML_PARSE_NOENT (65c5864d7fac) stayed in.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 added XML_PARSE_HUGE, which lifts libxml2's size limits. This patch adds XML_PARSE_NOENT and keeps the default limits, and the row records that the earlier switch to XML_PARSE_NOENT stayed in.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "Add support for parsing of large XML data (>= 10MB)"
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit 2197d06224a1, following a discussion over a Coverity
report where issues like the "Billion laugh attack" could cause the
backend to waste CPU and memory even if a client applied checks on the
size of the data given in input, and libxml2 does not offer guarantees
that input limits are respected under XML_PARSE_HUGE.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P15 reverted XML_PARSE_HUGE because libxml2 gives no input-limit guarantees under that flag. This patch does not touch XML_PARSE_HUGE, so libxml2's default entity limits still apply.

objections.title: Bugfix tag conflicts with a fix that changes query results
objections.failure_scenario: If the fix is back-patched, a minor release silently changes XMLTABLE and xpath() output for existing applications. If it is not back-patched, any user on a supported branch who sends a crafted document still gets a backend that ignores cancel and needs kill -9 and a restart.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix and targets 19, but message #1 does not say what happens on back branches. The fix for the hang also redefines which tree XPath sees, so two different changes are bundled together. A committer would likely want them separated: a narrow fix for the uncancellable loop that is safe to back-patch, and the semantic change done in master only, with documentation.
objections.author_must_show: What fix do back branches get for the uncancellable loop that leaves current xpath() and XMLTABLE results unchanged?

critic.reasoning: The entry is tagged Bugfix, and message #1 says results change but does not name the branches. The material does not show that a narrower fix exists, so the request to split the patch is a question for the author, not a requirement.

objections.title: Changed xpath() results go stale in expression indexes and stored columns
objections.failure_scenario: A site has an expression index or a stored generated column on xpath() or xmlexists() over documents that declare internal entities. pg_upgrade carries the old index entries and stored values over unchanged. Index scans then disagree with recomputed results, for example missing rows whose text now reads "uy", until someone finds the cause and runs REINDEX.
objections.argument: Message #1 states that results change for documents with entity references. xpath() and xmlexists() are, as far as I know, marked immutable, so users may have built indexes and generated columns on them. The commit message lists no documentation change and no release-note or upgrade guidance. The claim that documents without entity references are not affected is true, but it does not help users who do have them.
objections.author_must_show: Will the patch document the change as an incompatibility and tell users with xpath() or xmlexists() indexes or generated columns to reindex or recompute after upgrade?

critic.reasoning: xpath() and xmlexists() are immutable, and stored xml values keep their entity references, so an expression index over such documents can hold old results after upgrade. The case is rare, but the patch has no documentation or upgrade note for it.

objections.title: Fix avoids one libxml2 loop but leaves backends uncancellable
objections.failure_scenario: A user runs a different XPath expression that hits another libxml2 traversal bug, or the same bug through a tree shape that NOENT does not remove. The backend again ignores cancel, statement_timeout and pg_terminate_backend(). The DBA finds out only when kill -9 forces a cluster restart.
objections.argument: Message #1 names the root cause as a probable bug in xmlXPathNextFollowing and says the investigation into interrupt handling inside libxml2 is still open. The patch removes the entity reference nodes that trigger this one case. It does not bound how long the backend can run inside libxml2 without checking for interrupts. A committer would likely ask whether the project is signing up to patch around each libxml2 traversal bug in turn, with nothing that fails loudly when a new one appears.
objections.author_must_show: Can xmlXPathNextFollowing loop on any tree without entity reference nodes, and is there a plan to keep backends cancellable during long libxml2 calls?

critic.reasoning: The fix depends on no entity reference nodes staying in the tree, and the material does not show this for references libxml2 cannot resolve. The general worry about other libxml2 bugs has no concrete scenario and should not carry the objection.

refuted.title: Changed xpath() results leave existing expression indexes inconsistent
refuted.failure_scenario: A user has a stored generated column, check constraint, partition key or expression index built on xpath() or xmlexists() over documents with internal entities, then runs pg_upgrade or a patched minor release. The stored values and index entries keep the old results while new evaluations return the expanded ones. Index scans and sequential scans then return different rows, and nothing reports it.
refuted.argument: xpath() and xmlexists() are immutable, so users may store their results or index them. Message #1 states that results change for documents with entity references, for example {u} becomes {uy}. The commit message has no release-note guidance asking users to rebuild dependent indexes or recheck stored values. The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, so a backpatch is plausible, and a backpatch would also put patched and unpatched nodes in the same physical replication setup.
refuted.author_must_show: Will this stay master-only, with a release note telling users to reindex and recheck stored xpath()/xmlexists() results over documents with entity references?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The added point about mixed minor versions in physical replication depends on a backpatch that the proposal does not ask for.

refuted.title: Unprivileged backend hang stays in back branches after this fix
refuted.failure_scenario: On a supported release, any role allowed to call xpath() runs the query from message #1. The backend ignores cancel, statement_timeout and pg_terminate_backend(). The operator finds out when the backend holds its locks and snapshot until someone uses kill -9, which restarts the whole cluster.
refuted.argument: Message #1 shows that a plain SELECT is enough to trigger the loop, with no privileges beyond EXECUTE on xpath(). The fix avoids the trigger by changing query results, so a committer would likely hesitate to backpatch it, and the proposal does not say whether it is meant for back branches. The patch also leaves the backend unable to service interrupts while it runs inside libxml2, so any other construct that loops there still leads to a cluster restart.
refuted.author_must_show: What mitigation for the uncancellable loop could go into back branches without changing xpath() results, or why is a master-only fix acceptable for this denial of service?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2 for the back-branch question and of maintenance-fit-1 for the missing interrupt handling inside libxml2. The privilege point adds weight to those two but no separate failure.

refuted.title: Bugfix tag conflicts with changed query results in back branches
refuted.failure_scenario: If the fix is back-patched, an application that reads /r/text() on documents with internal entities gets {uy} instead of {u} after a minor upgrade. If it is not back-patched, supported branches keep the uncancellable loop with no mitigation.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, but message #1 and the commit message both say results change for documents with entity references. The proposal does not say which branches it targets. It also has no documentation hunk for the new xpath(), xmlexists() and XMLTABLE behaviour. Back branches need either a version that does not change results or an explicit decision to leave them exposed.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this meant for back branches, and if so, how will users who rely on the current entity-reference results be warned in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which states the same back-branch conflict and says what a committer would ask for.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Changed xpath() and xmlexists() results can differ from values already held in expression indexes and stored generated columns.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: xmlexists() and XMLTABLE are SQL/XML features, and their results change for documents with entity references.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Any role that can call xpath() can start the uncancellable loop, and the patch adds entity expansion to two more parse calls.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix, but the fix changes query results and message #1 names no branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The fix works around a probable libxml2 bug in xmlXPathNextFollowing, an interface the project does not control.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: see objection maintenance-fit-1: Fix avoids one libxml2 loop but leaves backends uncancellable

questions: Which branches is the patch meant for, and what do back branches get for the uncancellable loop if the result change stays in master only?
Will the patch document the changed results as an incompatibility and tell users to reindex expression indexes and recompute stored columns built on xpath() or xmlexists()?
Can entity reference nodes still reach XPath evaluation after the patch, for example for references that libxml2 cannot resolve?
Which libxml2 versions show the loop in xmlXPathNextFollowing?
Is there a plan to keep backends cancellable during long libxml2 calls, or is that out of scope for this patch?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the libxml2 integration in xml.c and the back-patch policy for fixes that change results. None has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for changed xpath(), xmlexists() and XMLTABLE results on documents with entity references, for the branch decision, and for any libxml2 loop this workaround does not cover.
committability.author_follow_up: The author says in message #1 that he will investigate the libxml2 bug and report it. There is no other sign either way.

priority.reason: Few documents use internal entities, but any role that can call xpath() can force a cluster restart (message #1). The patch is 4.2 KiB, touches xml.c and its regression test, and reuses a flag xml_parse() already passes.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody can confirm that XML_PARSE_HUGE stays off and that the external entity loader in xml.c covers these two parse calls. The claim that no entity reference nodes stay in the tree also needs a check against the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add table expansion hook
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a planner hook that lets an extension replace or wrap expand_inherited_rtentry(), so it can do its own table expansion and partition pruning. TimescaleDB and HypoPG wanted it because Postgres 12 moved expansion to a later point, where the get_relation_info hook could no longer control it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane doubted that an extension could replace expand_inherited_rtentry() without copying large parts of the mostly static code in inherit.c, and he asked for a worked-out example of the hook in use. Amit Langote added that the v12 and later expansion code adds row identity and junk columns, which a replacement would also have to reproduce. No example arrived and the thread was inactive after May 2021, so Jaime Casanova returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Would it be unreasonable of us to ask for a worked-out example making
use of the proposed hook?  That'd go a long way towards resolving the
question of whether you can do anything useful without duplicating
lots of code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add "\gi file" to psql to allow COPY with variable expansion
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first let psql's \copy expand :-variables in table and file names. After Tom Lane objected to the implementation, it became a new \gi file (or \gi command|) meta-command that sends a SQL COPY ... FROM STDIN with input from a file or program, and \copy was rewritten on top of the \g and \gi code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The cfbot tests for the \gi patch failed for weeks, and the cfbot log included a core dump. Andres Freund reported this on 2025-05-13, and no fixed version was posted. He marked the entry returned with feedback on 2025-06-17.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: However, the tests have not passed in quite a while:

precedents_retrieved.title: Added support of XML_PARSE_HUGE flag for XML documents
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch passes the libxml2 XML_PARSE_HUGE flag when Postgres parses XML, which raises the single text node limit from 10,000,000 to 1,000,000,000. It replaces xmlParseBalancedChunkMemory(), which takes no options, with xmlNewNode() plus xmlParseInNodeContext() on a fake root node, and moves from xmlParseMemory() to xmlReadMemory().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The XML_PARSE_HUGE change was committed to HEAD as 2197d06224a1 and then reverted in f2743a7d70e7. The security team found that it lets the backend use large amounts of CPU and memory in cases like the billion laughs attack, even when the application checks input size, because libxml2 does not guarantee input limits under XML_PARSE_HUGE. The author agreed with the revert. The separate replacement of xmlSubstituteEntitiesDefault() with XML_PARSE_NOENT (65c5864d7fac) stayed in.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The security team has discussed 2197d06224a1 after a report from coverity regarding the effects that issues like [1] would create in the backend, and concluded that this patch should be reverted because this could cause the backend to waste plently of CPU and/or memory even if the application applied checks on the size of the data given in input, and libxml2 does not offer guarantees that input limits are respected under XML_PARSE_HUGE.

precedents_retrieved.title: pgbench: allow to cancel queries during benchmark
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgbench send cancel requests to all connections on Ctrl+C, so long-running benchmark queries do not keep running on the backend after pgbench exits. On non-Windows, thread #0 handles SIGINT and cancels queries for all clients through a global array of client states.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO said thread #0 cancelling clients that other threads manage can cause race conditions, and asked that each thread cancel its own clients. In message #19 the author found two more problems: thread #0 cannot cancel anything once it leaves its loop, and with -C each thread recreates its PGcancel objects while thread #0 reads them. Alvaro Herrera then said commit 61461a300c1c, which deprecated PQcancel, requires the patch to be reworked. The author planned a redesign, but the visible messages show no new version.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Due to commit 61461a300c1c, this patch needs to be reworked.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restart pg_usleep when interrupted
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a sleep function, later named pg_usleep_non_interruptible, that restarts nanosleep() with the remaining time when a signal interrupts it, and stops once the requested time has passed. Vacuum cost delay would use it so the parallel vacuum leader sleeps the full delay even when parallel workers send it frequent progress messages.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry after the thread questioned whether the extra code was worth it. Nathan Bossart noted that interrupts rarely hit a vacuum delay point and that rate-limiting worker progress reports to 1 Hz would remove most of them, and the uninterruptible sleep would make vacuum slower to react to SIGTERM or cancel. CF #5118 would also change how pg_usleep() handles these interrupts, so the author left the question to that work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Is it really that important to delay with that level of accuracy?

precedents_retrieved.title: Infinite Autovacuum loop caused by failing virtual generated column expression
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes ANALYZE skip an extended statistics object, with a WARNING, when evaluating one of its expressions raises an error, instead of failing for the whole table. The goal was to stop autovacuum from retrying a failing ANALYZE every cycle, as happens with extended statistics on an erroring virtual generated column.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed and Bharath Rupireddy saw the behaviour as expected: it has existed since expression statistics arrived in PG14, retries come about once a minute, a later retry may succeed, and the user can drop or fix the statistics object. Bharath also said a fix only for extended statistics is inconsistent with how autovacuum handles other ANALYZE errors. He found that v2 catches the error without re-throwing or aborting a subtransaction, which can leave an inconsistent state such as a non-empty SPI stack. He then withdrew the patch from the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: After thinking about this more, I still prefer leaving the behaviour as-is (option 1).

precedents_retrieved.title: Cancel problems of query to pg_stat_statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_stat_statements queries cancellable by adding interrupt checks inside the read loop of qtext_load_file, which loads the query text file, and by cutting the read chunk size from 1GB to 32MB so the checks run more often. Because the function can run while pgss->lock is held, v2 only records that an interrupt is pending inside the loop and calls CHECK_FOR_INTERRUPTS after the loop ends and the lock is released.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrey Borodin first noted that the lock held during the file read blocks interrupts anyway; v2 worked around that. Michael Paquier then rejected the patch as only a workaround for a larger problem: the on-disk PGSS query text file does not scale once it is large and entries turn over often. He pointed instead to a planned rework that would move pg_stat_statements onto the pgstats API as a custom stats kind, with the query texts held entirely in memory.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch is only a workaround for a larger problem: the PGSS text
file does not and will never scale once it reaches a large size and
once we have a high turnover rate of the PGSS entries due to different
query IDs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't ignore recovery conflict interrupt on blocked writing
precedents_retrieved.summary: On a standby, a backend blocked writing results to a stuck or dead client ignores interrupts, so its buffer pin can block WAL replay until the TCP retransmission timeout, which can be about 15 minutes. The patch makes ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() handle recovery conflict interrupts during a blocked write and terminate the session, with a new Perl module for raw protocol tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch did not promote the ERROR to FATAL, so the session was not really terminated. He also showed that the backend often reaches ProcessClientWriteInterrupt() with interrupts held, for example while sending an error message, and then the conflict is never resolved. The author posted a reworked approach on 2025-01-21. No reply follows in the visible messages, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Unfortunately I suspect that this means any protection we'd get from this version of the patch is rather incomplete - if the recovery conflict is triggered while not blocked, we'll ERROR out and report the message with interrupts held.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent records a rejection of XML_PARSE_NOENT. The only related reason, entity-expansion DoS, was tied to XML_PARSE_HUGE, which this patch does not add. xml_parse() already expands entities with this flag, as message #1 shows, so the reason does not carry over. Back-branch policy for the changed results is a question for other angles.
Two fixable objections. Aligning with xml_parse() and contrib/xml2 matches existing practice, so consistency counts in the patch's favour.
The patch touches no WAL, catalog, wire protocol or ABI. Its only persistent effect is through stored or indexed results of immutable functions, which the objection covers.

External entities and expansion size give no objection, because xml input already parses with XML_PARSE_NOENT, so expanding entities again in xpath() adds no new exposure. This assumes the patch keeps XML_PARSE_HUGE off, unlike [P3] and [P15], and that the external entity loader in xml.c still covers these parse calls; both need confirming in the code.

The core change copies existing practice in xml_parse() and contrib/xml2, so a separate fit objection is weak. Input documents already pass entity expansion in xml_in, which limits any new expansion cost on these paths.

No existing feature does this job. Re-parsing through xmlserialize gives the expanded tree, but it does not stop any user from hanging an uncancellable backend with plain xpath(). The patch reuses the flag xml_parse() and contrib/xml2 already use, so it extends existing practice and adds no second mechanism.

This is a bugfix, so field demand is the wrong test. Any user who can run xpath() on a short crafted document can start a backend loop that ignores cancel, statement_timeout and pg_terminate_backend(), and only a restart stops it (message #1). The changed results affect only documents with entity references, so their users bear the cost. Whether the fix should be backpatched, and whether XML_PARSE_NOENT is safe here (see [P3], [P15]), belong to other angles.
